Ethan —

Great to hear — this is squarely in our ISV integrations lane. Quick answers up front, then a suggested playbook we can iterate on: 

- Tracing: we prefer OpenTelemetry spans with a small Redwood convention for model_id / runtime_variant tags. That keeps traces portable across our console and customers' APMs. We can accept either OTel or a lightweight shim that emits equivalent fields.
- Prompt/tool hooks: LangChain and LlamaIndex both have callback hooks we recommend instrumenting. For LangChain use the "CallbackManager" pattern; for LlamaIndex instrument the Query/Retriever call paths so tool calls show up in the same trace. 
- Embedding / caching: ensure deterministic tokenization for the embedding input (trim whitespace, normalize unicode). We also recommend including a model-version tag in cache keys.

Suggested integration playbook (attachments: draft-integration-playbook.md, signalweave-compat-matrix.csv):
1) Compatibility matrix: map LangChain & LlamaIndex versions -> supported adapter APIs -> required tracing fields.
2) Small tracing shim: reference OTel, but provide a fallback Redwood attribute mapping.
3) Prompt-tool contract: list of events (prompt_start, prompt_end, tool_call, tool_return) to emit.
4) QA checklist: end-to-end traces, console visualization, cost regression checks.
5) Security/SC questions: handoff to security for SOC 2 checklist (Ruth at SignalWeave added below).

Can we aim for a technical sync early next week? I’ll loop in product & SDK leads (cc’d).

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear playbook. A couple of security/compliance items from our side before we finalize the SOW: 

- SOC2 / Data handling: attaching our questionnaire (signalweave-soc2-questions.pdf). Could you confirm where traces are persisted and whether any PII could be present in prompt inputs when traces are exported?
- Keys/credentials: our customers expect adapter integrations to support per-tenant API keys; are there recommended KMS patterns on the Redwood side we should document in the playbook?
- Minimal viable trace payload: we prefer that SDKs can optionally redact prompt text in traces and still preserve timing/structure for debugging. Is a redaction flag feasible?

Quick answers to your earlier points: the OTel preference works for us; if Redwood can provide a small example shim (node + python) that demonstrates the event contract you describe, that would accelerate customer adoption.

Ruth Chen
Head of Security, SignalWeave
ruth.security@signalweave.ai
